notes: National Rail (Darwin/OpenLDBWS) is structurally catalogued here but blocked at the account level — DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN not set. Same blocker as every other UK region in this pipeline.

HUB + SECONDARY-HUB architecture, reused from West of England (Bristol Temple Meads/Bath Spa) and Solent (Southampton Central alone, Portsmouth Harbour/Portsmouth & Southsea pair) — NOT full flat multi-group. Reading (RDG) is the hub lock: single flat board, three operators (GWR/CrossCountry/SWR), no internal doNotGroup (report line 36 explicitly rules out multi-operator platform mixing at Reading).

Oxford (OXF) is the secondary hub, but UNLIKE Bath Spa/Portsmouth & Southsea it needs an internal doNotGroup split: GWR main line and Chiltern Railways' Marylebone branch sit on separate platforms/infrastructure at Oxford and require separate boarding logic per operator (report line 16, 37, 56, C2/C3 point 4/6) — first time in this pipeline a SECONDARY hub (not a primary terminus) has needed this. Enforced the same way as London Bridge/Liverpool Street in london-se-national-rail: two catalog entries sharing one physical CRS (OXF), split by operator, groupId 'oxford', doNotGroup: true, each carrying its own operators list passed as includeOperators to the shared uk-darwin.js fetchStationBoard().

Single agency (National Rail, four TOCs total across the region), single mode (train). No buses, no light rail, no trams, no Elizabeth Line (TfL, separate mode/operator, out-mode at Reading per report C2/C3 point 7). No Eurostar, no sleeper services named in this report's scope — no excludeOperators needed anywhere in this catalog.

Five through-running-only stations, none merge/hub candidates at D1: Swindon (SWI, GWR main-line continuation upstream of the Westbury boundary), Banbury (BAN, Chiltern + GWR on separate infrastructure at the same town, not a hub, proposed doNotGroup only if ever promoted — not built as a stationGroup), Westbury (WSB, boundary to West of England/Solent, already flagged reciprocally in both those regions' finished packs), Henley-on-Thames (HEY, GWR branch, single operator), Didcot Parkway (DID, GWR main line, Cotswold Line connection point, single operator).

London Paddington (PAD) and London Marylebone (MYB) are boundary-only references to London & South East National Rail's catalog — Paddington is already built there as a stationGroup, Marylebone is explicitly not built there either. Neither is built here; not present in this stops array.

CRS codes (RDG, OXF, SWI, BAN, WSB, HEY, DID) are carried from the oracle report's tables and are NOT verified against a live GTFS dump or Darwin response — crsVerified: false throughout, confirm before relying on them for a live board.

Direction model: destination + operator, matching every other UK National Rail region's recommendation. At Oxford this applies within each of the two doNotGroup sections (GWR section, Chiltern section), not across them. No line+terminus model — neither GWR nor Chiltern brand this corridor with named lines on a departure board. Illustrative only, not verified against a live Darwin payload. See docs/thames-valley-d1/direction-model-memo.md.

SKIP RISK — Chiltern Railways operator transition from Arriva to DfT Operator on 20 September 2026 (report skip risk 3): not a blocker, but a timing flag for whoever wires the token after that date — verify Darwin correctly attributes Chiltern services and any operator/agency mapping reflects the new operator structure.

stops.class: hub lock — principal rail terminus and interchange for Thames Valley, 15 platforms. Three operators but single flat destination+operator board (report line 36: no multi-operator platform mixing at Reading, unlike Oxford).

Secondary hub, subordinate to Reading on the same corridor.
